bullets.text: The NES Collection's Curator's Note and first two chapters are now fully hand-written! While I was at it, a fresh research pass caught a few wrong game titles and release years.
PAL badges: NES cards now show "PAL-adjusted" or "PAL-optimised", so you can see at a glance which games actually got some love for 50Hz. The filter finds those labels too.
The Game Boy Collection's Curator's Note is now hand-written as well.
Navigation bar: a persistent bar at the top of every page, so you can jump to any part of the project from anywhere.
Dark/light toggle: always in the top right corner now, whatever page you're on.
Back to top: on large screens, a button appears once you've scrolled down. Phones don't get one, because tapping the top of the screen already does the trick.
Chapters drop-down: replaces the chapter chips. It's cleaner on every screen size and better for accessibility. You can now also link straight to a chapter, e.g. `/nes/#ch-3`.
Previous / next: every Collection now ends with links to its neighbours on the shelf, for when you just want to keep browsing.
Footer: tidied up, with direct links to the AI disclaimer and privacy policy on the How it's made page.
Screen readers: the whole project is now fully usable with them.
Keyboard: navigation is much improved, and every page now has a skip link. More improvements are on the way!
Colour: this one's tricky, since the project leans heavily on artistic use of colour. Accessibility matters to me, though, so high-contrast and colourblind modes are on my list.

sections.text: And as always, lots of tiny visual fine-tuning. :D

bullets.text: In the Game Boy Collection, I swapped in Castlevania II: Belmont's Revenge for Solomon's Club. I forgot to add an actual Castlevania game to the chapter on Metroidvania! :D I also found Solomon's Club redundant because block puzzlers are already well represented in the Collection, and it has no unique regional or historical story.

The How it's made page is now available. Here you can learn about who I am, how I create, improve and maintain this project. I also find it very important to be 100% transparent on the use of AI, how I measure site views, my zero-tracking policy, as well as possible ways to financially support the project in the future. Check it out if you get the chance, I appreciate it!

Version history is now dynamic: To support a fun new dynamic release timeline graphic, as well as a possible notification service or Discord bot in the future, I converted the version history from static HTML to JSON data.
Added "Hand-written" / "Draft in progress" badges on the hub and on every Collection page.
Fonts are now self-hosted, so visitor IP addresses no longer go to Google.
The "Report a mistake" email links now fill in the page name in the subject line.
Several styling improvements: Site navigation has improved both on desktop and mobile browsers. Fine-tuned the platform flourishes for the Game Boy, SNES and DS.

3 new collections added: The Nintendo DS, Sega Master System and Microsoft Xbox Collections are now live. They were researched and styled with Claude Cowork (Sonnet 5, High effort), same as before. I'll be rewriting their stories myself over time, just like the original twelve.

Styling overhaul: Pushing the styling intensity on the 3 new collections made them noticeably bolder than the original set, so I brought that same energy back to the base collections and the hub page.
sub: CSS cleanup across every theme: 13 theme stylesheets and the hub stylesheet had leftover duplicate code from the styling passes, now consolidated with no visual changes.
Added a graphical timeline to the hub page, with clickable platform markers.
A handful of smaller styling fixes and tweaks throughout.

bullets.text: Simple CMS support: Added GitHub Pages CMS by Ronan Berder, so I can add and edit content without touching the code.
sub: Data format migration: required converting all 12 original platforms' game lists from arrays to named objects.
